name: p1-refused-zipdma-two-channel-behavior
description: Refusal sample: the same pinned ZipDMA and four-word block, but the behavior file declares two channels, an eight-byte beat, two outstanding requests and a four-beat burst. The planner refuses the declaration against its pinned device facts by name.
notes: This scenario exists to record the planner refusal, not to pass: the pinned ZipDMA has one channel, a 32-bit beat, one outstanding request and no master burst.

The refusal is dma-capability-beyond-device:channels:2>1 (then the beat, outstanding and burst facts), raised by myfuzz.composition.dma_transfer.dma_transfer_declaration before any transfer is planned.
No multi-channel, wide-beat or multiple-outstanding execution is claimed anywhere: the RTL cannot encode it and the host does not run it.
